title: Window can't be closed on Wayland: Alt+F4 and the close button do nothing
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
**What happens**

On Wayland the ArtCraft Launcher window can't be closed. Alt+F4 and the title bar's close button both do nothing: the window stays open and keeps working.

**Steps**

1. Start ArtCraft Launcher on a Wayland session with a tray available (KDE Plasma here).
2. Leave "Keep running in the tray when the window is closed" on (the default).
3. Press Alt+F4, or click the close button.

Expected: the window goes away and the launcher stays in the tray.
Actual: nothing changes. The only way out is "Quit ArtCraft Launcher" in the tray menu.

**Cause**

`apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs` cancels the close request and then hides the window:

```rust
ctx.send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::CancelClose);
self.hide(ctx); // ViewportCommand::Visible(false)
```

egui-winit turns `Visible(false)` into `window.set_visible(false)`, and winit 0.30.13 does nothing for that call on Wayland (`platform_impl/linux/wayland/window/mod.rs`):

```rust
pub fn set_visible(&self, _visible: bool) {
    // Not possible on Wayland.
}
```

So the close is cancelled and the hide never happens. `Shell.visible` is also set to `false` while the window is still on screen, so the next click on the tray icon "shows" a window that was never hidden.

**System**

- ArtCraft Launcher 0.1.0 (`.deb`), also read against `main` at b642df2
- Ubuntu 26.04.1, KDE Plasma 6.6.6, Wayland, x86_64

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: A failed install deletes the verified download, so retrying downloads from zero
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
**What happens**

When the install step fails after a download has finished and passed its checksum, the launcher deletes the downloaded file. Trying again downloads the whole file from zero.

The install step fails for reasons that have nothing to do with the file: the password prompt is dismissed, another package manager holds the lock, the app is running. These files are 100 MB and more.

**Steps**

1. Install any app on Linux with the `.deb` format.
2. Let the download finish, then dismiss the password prompt.
3. Press Install again.

Expected: the verified file is used again and only the install step runs.
Actual: the download starts over at 0%.

**Cause**

`crates/native/src/install.rs`, at the end of `install()`:

```rust
// The download has served its purpose either way; a failed install starts fresh next time.
let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&file);
```

The file is removed on success and on failure alike.

**Proposal**

- Keep the verified file when the install step fails, and delete it only after a successful install.
- On the next Install, check the kept file against the published SHA-256 again and skip the download when it matches. A file that no longer matches is discarded and fetched again, as today.
- Show that state in the UI: "Retry install" as the main action, with "Download again" in the menu to throw the file away.
- The existing 30-day cleanup of the downloads folder (`http::clean_downloads`) already bounds how long a kept file stays.

**System**

- ArtCraft Launcher 0.1.0 (`.deb`), read against `main` at b642df2
- Ubuntu 26.04.1, KDE Plasma 6.6.6, Wayland, x86_64

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Installing several apps at once: all but the first fail with "error 100"
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
**What happens**

When several apps are installing at once (for example with "Update all"), only the first one installs. It opens the password prompt, and while that prompt is open every other install fails with "the system installer stopped with error 100".

**Steps**

1. On Linux with the `.deb` format, start two or more installs so their downloads run together.
2. Wait until they reach "Installing…". The first one opens the password prompt.
3. Leave the prompt open, or type the password.

Expected: every app installs, with one password prompt.
Actual: the first app installs. The others fail with error 100 and have to be started again, one at a time.

**Cause**

`NativeBackend::start_job` in `crates/native/src/backend.rs` runs each install on its own thread. On Linux each thread ends in `run_as_root` (`crates/native/src/install.rs`), which starts its own `pkexec apt-get install -y …`.

Two things follow:

- Only one process can hold the dpkg lock. A second `apt-get` that can't take it exits with code 100, which the launcher reports as "the system installer stopped with error 100".
- Each `pkexec` call authenticates separately, so even run one after another there would be one password prompt per app.

The same applies to `dnf`, `zypper` and `rpm` installs, and to uninstalls, which go through `run_as_root` too.

**Proposal**

- Run the privileged step of installs one at a time: jobs that reach "Installing…" wait in a queue instead of failing.
- Install the packages that are ready together in one privileged call (`apt-get install a.deb b.deb`), so the password is asked for once.

**System**

- ArtCraft Launcher 0.1.0 (`.deb`), read against `main` at b642df2
- Ubuntu 26.04.1, KDE Plasma 6.6.6, Wayland, x86_64

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: UI tests segfault intermittently when run in parallel
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
**What happens**

The UI tests (`crates/ui-egui/tests/ui.rs`) sometimes end with a segmentation fault when they run in parallel, which is how `cargo test` and `cargo xtask ci` run them. The process exits with signal 11 partway through: in the three crashes below, 8, 5 and 5 of the 11 tests had printed `ok`.

**Numbers**

On `main` at e8c4b3d, running the built test binary directly:

| How | Runs | Crashed |
|---|---|---|
| Default (parallel threads) | 40 | 3 (exit status 139) |
| `--test-threads=1` | 20 | 0 |

```sh
cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-ui-egui --no-run
for i in $(seq 40); do target/debug/deps/ui-<hash> >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "run $i: $?"; done
```

A crashed run prints no panic message and no `test result:` summary.

**Likely cause**

`harness()` builds an `egui_kittest` harness with `.wgpu()` for every test, so each test thread creates and tears down its own wgpu device at the same time as the others. The crash goes away when the tests run one at a time. I have not got a backtrace yet.

**Where I have seen it**

- Locally only: Ubuntu 26.04.1, Mesa 26.0.8, AMD Radeon 890M (RADV), 20 threads.
- Not in this repository's CI so far: the two failed CI runs in the history are the formatting check, not this.

It still costs contributors a failed `cargo xtask ci` roughly one run in ten on hardware like mine.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: [Windows] 0.1.2 portable crashes on launch in igvk64.dll (Intel UHD 620 Vulkan driver)
author: hungry-detective
body:
## Summary
`artcraft-launcher-0.1.2-windows-x64-portable\artcraft-launcher.exe` crashes immediately on launch with no window. Faulting module is the Intel Vulkan driver `igvk64.dll`. Same crash affects FilmCraft portable (`filmcraft.exe` 0.4.0 and 0.5.0) on the same machine at the same fault offset.

## Repro
1. Unzip `artcraft-launcher-0.1.2-windows-x64-portable.zip`
2. Double-click `artcraft-launcher.exe` (or run `artcraft-launcher.exe --help` from PowerShell)
3. Nothing opens, process exits with `-1073741819` (`0xC0000005`)

## Environment
- App: ArtCraft Launcher 0.1.2 portable, `artcraft-launcher.exe` FileVersion 0.1.2, size 21434248 bytes
- OS: Windows 11 Pro `10.0.26300` x64-based PC (HP laptop, BIOS Q85 v01.31.00)
- GPU: `Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620`, DriverVersion `31.0.101.2140`
- Faulting driver: `C:\WINDOWS\System32\DriverStore\FileRepository\iigd_dch.inf_amd64_65ac4d73bb85cb27\igvk64.dll`, same version `31.0.101.2140`

## Event Viewer (Application Error, ID 1000, repeated)
```
Faulting application name: artcraft-launcher.exe, version: 0.1.2.0, time stamp: 0x6aca2397
Faulting module name: igvk64.dll, version: 31.0.101.2140, time stamp: 0x690b539d
Exception code: 0xc0000005
Fault offset: 0x000000000064ea82
Faulting module path: ...\iigd_dch.inf_amd64_65ac4d73bb85cb27\igvk64.dll
```
Identical offset `0x64ea82` + `0xc0000005` for `filmcraft.exe` 0.4.0/0.5.0 on same PC.

Forcing DirectX keeps it running:
```powershell
$env:WGPU_BACKEND="dx12"

title: [macOS] Crashes on launch with OpenCore Legacy Patcher: "invalid value 'metal3.2'" (workaround inside)
author: Davidadragoo
body:
**What happens**
On macOS, the launcher window flashes for a moment and then the app quits immediately.

**System**
- ArtCraft Launcher v0.1.0 (macos-universal.dmg)
- macOS Sequoia 15.7.4, installed with OpenCore Legacy Patcher
- Mac: MacBook Pro 15" mid-2015

**Error (running the binary from Terminal)**
```
ERROR wgpu_core::indirect_validation] indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2' ... note: use 'metal3.1' for 'Metal 3.1' standard"))
ERROR eframe::native::run] Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
ERROR artcraft_launcher] WGPU error: Parent device is lost
```

**Likely cause**
The app picks the Metal shader language version from the macOS version (15 → Metal 3.2). On OpenCore-patched Macs, the legacy GPU drivers only support up to Metal 3.1, so shader compilation fails and the device is lost. Choosing the version based on what the GPU/driver actually supports, or falling back when 3.2 fails, would fix it.

**Workaround**
Launching with the system version compatibility flag works:
```
SYSTEM_VERSION_COMPAT=1 /Applications/ArtCraft\ Launcher.app/Contents/MacOS/*
```
The individual Craft apps may hit the same issue, since they use the same wgpu/eframe stack.

title: Every app shows "Not available here" / "Offline" on some Windows PCs (UnknownIssuer)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
A few users on Discord see every app in the launcher as "Not available here" with an "Offline" button. Reinstalling, restarting and switching wifi doesn't help. Hovering the badge shows:

    Couldn't check for updates: invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer

GitHub is fine and other PCs work, so it's local to those machines.

The launcher builds its trust store once from the Windows root store (rustls-native-certs in `crates/native/src/http.rs`). Windows doesn't ship every root up front. It adds them when something asks it to verify a chain. Chrome and Edge do their own verification, so a PC that only uses them can be missing the root GitHub's certificate needs. Antivirus HTTPS scanning can cause the same error.

Possible fix: let the OS verify the chain (rustls-platform-verifier, which ureq supports through its `platform-verifier` feature). PdfCraft's update check loads certificates the same way and probably has the same problem.

title: macOS installs don't check who signed the app or which version it is
author: s17sh70x2jfl031ag
body:
On macOS, `install_dmg` checks the download's SHA-256 and the app's bundle ID, then installs it. It never checks:

1. **Who signed it.** There's no `codesign` call in the install path (`crates/native/src/install.rs`, `copy_app`), so an unsigned app, or one signed by another developer, installs as long as it matches the release's checksum. Windows already pins the publisher (`Learning Machines LLC` in `detect.rs`). macOS has no equivalent yet.
2. **Which version it is.** `read_bundle` reads the app's version, but it's never compared with the release, so an older build published under a newer tag installs without complaint.

The checksum and the app come from the same release, so these checks only matter if a release is ever wrong or tampered with. That makes them defense in depth rather than a live hole. Self-update goes through the same `install_dmg`, so this covers the launcher too.

**Proposed fix**, small and offline:

- After the copy and before the swap, run `codesign --verify --deep -R '=anchor apple generic and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "DJ6XS33FX8"'` on the staged bundle. It accepts only a valid Developer ID signature from your team. Unlike `spctl`, it needs no network.
- Compare the bundle's version with the release's. A bundle that reports only `CFBundleShortVersionString` matches a pre-release with the same numbers, so `-rc` builds keep working.
- On failure, remove the staged copy and leave the installed one untouched.

I checked the current macOS releases of PhotoCraft 0.6.0, LightCraft 0.5.0, VectorCraft 0.8.0 and ArtCraft Launcher 0.1.3. All are signed by `DJ6XS33FX8`, and all still pass after the `ditto --noextattr` copy.

I have a PR ready with tests: unsigned and ad-hoc-signed bundles are refused, version matching (including pre-releases), and a refused update leaves the old copy alone. Two questions first:

1. Is `DJ6XS33FX8` the team for every Craft App, including ones not released yet?

title: Windows: Update all asks for permission once per app; make it one prompt, then install silently
author: KattKnight
body:
On Windows, **Update all** asks for administrator permission once per app, and each app's Windows Installer window opens in turn. Updating five apps means five UAC prompts and five progress windows, one after another, and the user has to sit through them. A user who updates the whole suite regularly asked for this to be one prompt, after which the updates happen in the background while they get on with something else.

## Why it happens

The Craft app MSIs install per machine (Program Files, HKLM), so each one needs elevation. `install::windows::run_msi` runs `msiexec /i <msi> /passive /norestart` for each app from the unelevated launcher, so Windows asks for permission every time. The `INSTALLER` queue (#6) makes those installs take turns, but each turn is still its own elevation.

## Proposal

One elevated helper per batch, which installs every waiting MSI silently:

1. **Collect the batch.** An MSI job downloads and verifies as now, then waits until no other MSI job is still downloading. Whatever is ready at that point becomes one batch, so **Update all** turns into one batch however long each download takes. A job that's cancelled or paused leaves the batch.
2. **Ask once.** The launcher starts itself elevated, once per batch: `artcraft-launcher.exe --install-msis <results file> <msi> <sha256> …`, through PowerShell's `Start-Process -Verb RunAs`, the same way `self_update.rs` already starts `msiexec`, so no `unsafe` code is needed. The UAC prompt names ArtCraft Launcher. Declining it cancels the batch, as a dismissed prompt does now.
3. **Install silently.** The helper runs `msiexec /i <msi> /qn /norestart` for each file in turn. No Windows Installer windows open, and the launcher shows each app's progress in its own window and tray as now.
4. **Report back.** The helper writes each MSI's exit code to the results file, and each job ends with its own result. One failed app doesn't fail the others.

title: [Security] Restrict feed-directed repositories and require checksums before install
author: kaboggs
body:
## Summary

I reviewed ArtCraft Launcher v0.2.0 (`bd1182e75c3e631ce877f7317b54b8243e2b4742`) and found two download-trust behaviors worth tightening. I have no evidence that the current feed or releases are compromised. This report describes conditional supply-chain risk.

### 1. The feed can redirect an app to any GitHub owner

`Feed::repo_for` follows `repo_renames` supplied by the network feed (`crates/core/src/feed.rs:128-138`). `RawRepoRename::into_rename` checks name syntax but does not constrain the new owner to `storytold` (`feed.rs:349-360`). The result is used for GitHub fallback (`crates/native/src/backend.rs:693-695`) and accepted as the prefix for release assets (`feed.rs:166-181`). The same path can affect the launcher's own release lookup.

If the feed were compromised, an attacker could point a Craft app to an attacker-owned GitHub repository and provide matching package metadata and hashes. The current URL-prefix and SHA-256 checks would still pass because both refer to the newly selected repository. Please consider pinning an approved owner/repository list, or verifying a migration independently before following a rename. Also bind each selected asset to the approved release tag.

### 2. An install can proceed when no checksum exists

`install::download` accepts `None` when release metadata and `SHA256SUMS.txt` have no digest (`crates/native/src/install.rs:140-165`). `http::matches_published` then checks only the file length (`crates/native/src/http.rs:393-398`). Self-update uses the same download path (`crates/native/src/self_update.rs:169-173`). A same-length altered package would pass that fallback. The user-visible note is added only after install succeeds (`crates/native/src/backend.rs:485-489`).

Please consider requiring a valid digest before install or self-update and showing an actionable error if it is unavailable. Platform code-signing identity checks would add a separate safeguard. I saw the related macOS signature discussion in #50.

body:
Currently, the Craft Apps Launcher requires administrator privileges (UAC elevation) not only when initially installing applications, but also whenever an installed application receives an update.

While requiring administrator privileges for the initial installation is understandable, requiring elevation for every subsequent update creates unnecessary friction, particularly in enterprise environments or on computers where users do not have local administrator privileges.

## Current Behavior

1. A user installs an application through the Craft Apps Launcher.
2. Windows requests administrator privileges during installation.
3. When an update becomes available, the launcher once again requests administrator privileges.

Ideally, administrator privileges should only be required during the initial installation or when absolutely necessary.

Subsequent application updates should be handled without requiring additional UAC elevation, allowing standard users to keep their applications up to date independently.

title: Flatpak bundle updates fail when app is already installed
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Description
When updating an already-installed application (or the launcher itself) using single-file Flatpak bundles (`.flatpak`), `flatpak install --user -y --noninteractive --bundle <file>` fails because Flatpak requires the `--reinstall` flag to install a bundle over an existing installation.

Without `--reinstall`, Flatpak exits with an error indicating that the application is already installed, and the update fails.

### Expected Behavior
Updating an installed Flatpak app via its bundle should reinstall/replace the installed version cleanly.

### Proposed Fix
Pass `--reinstall` to `flatpak install`, which allows reinstalling/updating when an existing build is present while still operating normally for clean installs.

title: Flatpak installation errors are masked by hardcoded Flathub remote message
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Description
In `crates/native/src/install.rs`, Flatpak bundle installations run via `cmd.status()`. If the command fails, the error message returned to the user is unconditionally hardcoded to:
`"Flatpak couldn't install the bundle (it needs the Flathub remote for its runtime)"`

This obscures the actual failure reason (such as bundle corruption, missing permissions, repo lock collision, or existing installation errors).

### Expected Behavior
The launcher should capture stderr/stdout from `flatpak install` and report the actual error message returned by Flatpak.

### Proposed Fix
Switch from `cmd.status()` to `cmd.output()` and extract the actual stderr string so users and logs see the true cause of failure.

title: Concurrent Flatpak bundle installs fail due to OSTree repo lock contention
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Description
When multiple Flatpak bundle installations are triggered concurrently (for example, when clicking 'Update All' or during automatic updates), background threads run multiple `flatpak install` processes at the same time.

Because each `flatpak install` must acquire the user's OSTree repository lock and configure local remotes, concurrent runs can collide on locks or exhaust sockets/network resolvers, causing installations to fail with errors such as `[6] Could not resolve hostname`.

### Expected Behavior
Flatpak bundle installations should be serialized rather than run uncoordinated across multiple threads.

### Proposed Fix
Run Flatpak bundle installs through the installation queue (`root.queue.alone`), ensuring each bundle install completes before the next begins.

title: Flatpak app detection matches wrong architecture when foreign-arch builds exist
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Description
In `crates/native/src/detect.rs`, installed Flatpak apps are enumerated using:
`flatpak list --app --columns=application,version,branch`
without specifying `--arch`.

If any foreign-architecture builds are present on the host (for example, an older `aarch64` build on an `x86_64` host), `flatpak list` returns rows for both architectures. The detector matches the first row returned for that application ID. If the outdated foreign-arch row is matched, the launcher continually detects the app as outdated and shows the 'Update' button even after a successful update of the host architecture build.

### Expected Behavior
Flatpak detection should only match installations whose architecture matches the host system architecture.

### Proposed Fix
Pass `--arch=<host_arch>` to `flatpak list` and `flatpak info` in detection queries.

title: Add console logging for launcher background actions and installer progress
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Description
Currently, running the launcher binary or Flatpak directly in a terminal (`flatpak run ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher`) provides minimal to no output on default settings because log levels default to `warn`. When an installation or update encounters background issues or stalls, the terminal output does not inform the user what action the launcher is executing.

### Expected Behavior
The launcher should log high-level status events (checking for updates, starting jobs, download completion, and installer commands) to the console at `info` level so users and packagers can diagnose behavior.

### Proposed Fix
Set default log filtering to `info` in `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs` and add structured `log::info` / `log::error` statements across installer and backend workflows.

title: Launcher spawns `pacman -Q` on non-Arch systems — opens the Pac-Man game where `pacman` is the game binary
author: Baptiste-Sys32
body:
## What happened

While ArtCraft Launcher v0.2.1 (Linux x86_64 AppImage) was running, the **Pac-Man arcade game** kept popping open on its own — no clicks, no updates in progress.

## Root cause

The launcher periodically shells out to `pacman -Q …` (presumably the Arch/AUR install detection). On Debian-family distros that check is wrong twice over: there is no Arch `pacman` here, and on my system `pacman` on `PATH` is `/usr/games/pacman` — the game. So every detection cycle launched the game with a `-Q` argument.

Process-tree evidence, captured live while the game window was open:

```
systemd(1)---artcraft-launch(9904)---pacman(10395)
```

`/proc/<pid>/cmdline` of the game process:

```
pacman -Q
```

So the launcher is the parent, invoking what it believes is the Arch package manager.

## Environment

- ArtCraft Launcher v0.2.1, `artcraft-launcher-0.2.1-linux-x86_64.AppImage` (SHA-256 verified)
- Linux Mint 22.3 (Ubuntu 24.04 base, x86_64), Cinnamon, X11
- `pacman` game package installed (`/usr/games/pacman` on default `PATH`)

## Expected behavior

The Arch/AUR detection should not blindly execute `pacman`:

- Gate it on the OS first (e.g. check `/etc/os-release` `ID`/`ID_LIKE` for `arch`), and/or
- Validate the binary before trusting it (e.g. `pacman --version` output looks like pacman, or the path is `pacman` the package manager, not `/usr/games/*`).

Any Debian/Ubuntu/Mint/Fedora user with an unrelated `pacman` on `PATH` hits this today; only Arch users benefit from the check.

## Workaround used

Uninstalled the game package (`apt remove pacman`, nothing depended on it). No game, no more popups — but the launcher is presumably still exec'ing a missing binary on every cycle.

Thanks for the launcher otherwise — the adopt-existing-installs behavior worked exactly as documented.

---
*Credit: caught together with my AI assistant (Muse Spark, via OpenCode) while it was helping me install the suite — it trapped the live process tree that proved the launcher was …

title: [App Proposal] PainterCraft: An open-source Substance 3D Painter alternative in Rust
author: HighOnBuffs
body:
Hey ArtCraft team!

I've been following the Craft suite, and it's genuinely exciting to see how quickly these applications are progressing.

One major missing piece in the creative pipeline, in my opinion, is a dedicated 3D texture painting application, something along the lines of Adobe Substance 3D Painter.

I'd love to see a project called PainterCraft.

Blender already gives us an excellent open-source 3D modeling environment, and PhotoCraft covers 2D image editing. But for professional PBR texturing, smart materials, baking, and painting directly onto 3D models, there's still a significant gap.

This would be especially valuable for game development, VRChat avatar creation, 3D artists, and VFX workflows.

What I'd love to see:

GPU-accelerated 3D painting with Rust and wgpu

Non-destructive material layers, masks and procedural generators

Smart materials, edge wear, dirt and curvature-based effects

PBR channels: base color, roughness, metallic, normal and height

Texture baking, UDIM support and Blender interoperability

Unity, Unreal and VRChat-friendly export presets

MCP and headless automation, allowing AI agents to work directly on materials

A particularly interesting feature would be an AI agent that could inspect a 3D model, create materials, apply realistic wear and export optimized textures automatically.

ArmorPaint could be useful inspiration for the overall workflow, while keeping the implementation independent and properly licensed.

Even a small MVP with mesh import, layered PBR painting and texture export would be a great starting point.

Are there already discussions or plans for something like this? I'd love to hear whether the team would consider adding it to the Craft suite.

Thanks for all the work you're putting into these projects!

title: [Bug] macOS Simplified Chinese interface displays as square boxes (Font fallback issue)
author: superlll082
body:
**Description**
When switching the interface language to Simplified Chinese (简体中文) on the macOS desktop app, all text displays as square boxes (□□) instead of actual characters. 

**Steps to Reproduce**
1. Open the PdfCraft macOS desktop app.
2. Go to Settings -> Language, and select "Simplified Chinese (简体中文)".
3. The interface immediately renders as square boxes. (Note: Switching to English or Traditional Chinese works fine).

**Root Cause Analysis**
According to the official documentation, macOS uses `Hiragino Sans` or `PingFang` for CJK languages. It appears that `Hiragino Sans` (which is primarily a Japanese font) is prioritized before `PingFang SC` in the CSS `font-family` fallback list. 

Since `Hiragino Sans` lacks many Simplified Chinese glyphs, macOS renders them as "tofu" boxes. 

**Suggested Fix**
Please reorder the CSS `font-family` fallback list for macOS to prioritize `PingFang SC` over `Hiragino Sans`, or explicitly map `zh-CN` / `zh-Hans` to use `PingFang SC` first. 

Example:
`font-family: 'PingFang SC', 'Hiragino Sans', ...`

**Environment**
- OS: macOS
- App Version: Latest Desktop Release

title: Linux settings: "Install new apps as" lists formats this system can't install, and a pick is silently ignored
author: tydude001
body:
**Settings → Installing on Linux → Install new apps as** always lists `.deb`, `.rpm`, Flatpak and AppImage, plus "System package (recommended)" for a launcher that isn't a Flatpak or an AppImage ([`dialogs.rs#L303-L308`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/blob/1aaf7b27be2dba970d1a77f96aef6aad52352730/crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs#L303-L308)). The list doesn't depend on what the system can install. When a new app is installed, `choose_kinds` drops a picked format that `available_kinds()` doesn't offer ([`install.rs#L131`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/blob/1aaf7b27be2dba970d1a77f96aef6aad52352730/crates/native/src/install.rs#L131)), so the install uses the default instead. Nothing fails, and nothing tells you the setting was ignored.

Since #107, this is most visible on Fedora Atomic. On Bazzite 44 with main at `1aaf7b2`, I called `available_kinds()` and `choose_kinds()` from a small example program, built against the library:

| launcher | offered | `.rpm` or `.deb` picked in settings |
|---|---|---|
| system install (not Flatpak or AppImage) | Flatpak, AppImage | Flatpak, AppImage |
| AppImage | AppImage, Flatpak | AppImage, Flatpak |
| same build in a Fedora 44 toolbox (not ostree), as a control | Rpm, Flatpak, AppImage | Rpm, Flatpak, AppImage |

So on Bazzite, going by `dialogs.rs` (I didn't open the dialog itself), a system-installed launcher shows "System package (recommended)" as its default when there is no system package to install, and new apps come as Flatpaks. Picking "RPM package (.rpm)" is accepted and makes no difference. The control row shows the same thing off ostree: on Fedora, picking `.deb` is listed and ignored too.

(Main's new `immutable_ostree_offers_no_deb_or_rpm` test passes on this host. It returns early wherever `/run/ostree-booted` is absent, so CI never really runs it.)

One possible fix would be to build the list from `available_kinds()`, and to label the default after its first entry instead of "System package".…

title: [Feature Request] Add Configurable Desktop and Start Menu Shortcuts for Each App

Please add comprehensive shortcut management to ArtCraft Launcher so users can control which shortcuts are created for each installed Craft app.

Current Behavior

I installed ArtCraft Launcher and installed PhotoCraft through it on Windows. PhotoCraft appears in the Start menu, but there is no desktop shortcut. I also cannot conveniently configure shortcut creation for individual applications through the launcher.

Expected Behavior

It would be great if ArtCraft Launcher provided centralized shortcut management with the following options:

1. Per-app shortcut management

- Choose whether to create a desktop shortcut for each application.
- Choose whether to create a Start menu shortcut for each application.
- Allow users to disable either shortcut independently or disable both.
- Allow users to create, remove, or restore shortcuts for already-installed applications without reinstalling them.

2. Global defaults and individual preferences

- Provide default shortcut preferences for all applications installed through the launcher.
- Allow individual applications to override these defaults.

title: [Feature Request] Start minimized and Start in system tray
author: edgarcnp
body:
### Summary

The ArtCraft Launcher already supports sitting in the system tray / menu bar, and you can open any Craft app from the tray icon. However, there is currently no way to control what happens when the launcher itself starts. I would like to request two startup options:

1. **Start minimized** — launch the app without showing the main window (minimized to the taskbar/dock).
2. **Start in system tray** — launch the app directly into the tray / menu bar, with no window shown at all.

### Proposed Solution

Add a **Startup** section to the Settings page with two checkboxes (or a dropdown):

- **Start minimized** — the main window opens minimized to the taskbar/dock.
- **Start in system tray** — the main window does not appear; only the tray icon is shown.

If possible, these two options could be mutually exclusive, or "Start in system tray" could simply imply "Start minimized" plus hiding the window entirely.

The setting should be persisted between runs, just like the existing language preference.

### Alternatives Considered

- A command-line flag (e.g. `--minimized` or `--tray`) could also work, but a persistent setting in the UI is more discoverable for regular users.
- Some launchers combine both behaviors into a single "Start minimized to tray" option. That would also solve the problem, though separate toggles give users more control.

### Additional Context

The launcher is already described as something that "can sit in your menu bar or system tray", and the tray icon is already functional. This request is only about controlling the startup behavior, not about adding tray support itself.

title: Windows launcher exits silently while a launcher runs inside WSL (single-instance port 47413 is forwarded by WSL2)
author: PistachioCannoli
body:
### What happens

With ArtCraft Launcher open inside WSL2 (the Linux AppImage, shown on the Windows desktop through WSLg), starting the Windows launcher does nothing: the process appears for a moment and exits with code 0. No window opens and there's no Event Viewer entry. What it actually does is bring the *WSL* launcher's window to the front, which is easy to miss.

If the Windows launcher is started first, the WSL launcher still starts fine and both run side by side.

### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (10.0.26200), x64, NVIDIA RTX 4080 SUPER
- WSL 2.3.26.0 in the default NAT networking mode (localhost forwarding on, which is the default), Ubuntu 24.04, WSLg 1.0.65
- ArtCraft Launcher 0.3.2 on both sides: `artcraft-launcher-0.3.2-windows-x64.msi` and `artcraft-launcher-0.3.2-linux-x86_64.AppImage`

### Steps to reproduce

1. In WSL, run the launcher AppImage and leave its window open.
2. In WSL: `ss -ltnp | grep 47413` shows `artcraft-launch` listening on `127.0.0.1:47413`.
3. On Windows, start `artcraft-launcher.exe` from the Start menu.
4. It exits within a second with code 0, and the WSL launcher's window comes forward.
5. Close the WSL launcher and start the Windows one again: it opens normally.

### Why

`crates/native/src/single_instance.rs` (at 1aaf7b2) claims the instance by binding the fixed loopback port `127.0.0.1:47413`. In WSL2's NAT mode, localhost forwarding mirrors a port that a Linux process listens on inside WSL onto the Windows host's loopback. The reverse direction doesn't collide: the Linux launcher binds inside WSL's own network namespace, and Windows listeners aren't forwarded into WSL.

The runtime is not involved: on macOS `native_options` passes an empty `IconData`, and eframe 0.36.2 skips `setApplicationIconImage` for it (`AppTitleIconSetter::new`). ### Fix Render the macOS icon (`.icns` and `artcraft-launcher-1024.png`) as the untouched mark on a light squircle tile laid out on Apple's 1024 grid: an 824 px tile with ~185 px corners. macOS then has nothing to add, and the icon matches before and after launch. Windows, Linux and BSD icons are unchanged.

title: [Feature Request] Delta updates: download only the blocks that changed (zsync for AppImages)
author: PanDuroDev
body:
## Motivation

Every Craft app ships a new release almost daily, and right now each update re-downloads the
full installer even for a tiny fix. Checked against v0.4.0: `install::download` always fetches the
whole asset and verifies its SHA-256. There is no incremental path, and `platform.rs`
deliberately skips the `.zsync` files that are already published next to every AppImage
(`packaging/linux/package.sh` generates them, and the README mentions them for AppImageUpdate).

## Proposal

Add delta updates for Linux AppImages first (the only format with ready-made delta metadata):

- When updating, fetch the release's `.zsync` control file and compare its per-block checksums
  (weak rolling checksum + truncated MD4) against the installed copy.
- Copy matching blocks from disk and download only the missing byte ranges (HTTP Range, which
  GitHub's CDN supports), then assemble the new file into a temporary path.
- Verify the assembled file against the release's published SHA-256 exactly like a full
  download. Rule #90 stays untouched: a file nothing vouches for is never installed.
- Any failure (no installed copy, no `.zsync` listed, range requests ignored, checksum
  mismatch) falls back to today's full download. Pause and cancel must propagate unchanged
  and never turn into a hidden full download.

## Why AppImage first

- The `.zsync` metadata is already published for every AppImage release, so no build-side
  change is needed to start.
- MSI/DMG/deb/rpm have no published delta metadata (pairwise patches like `.msp` or deltarpm
  would need per-version generation on top of daily releases), and Flatpak already deltas
  inside OSTree. They should stay full downloads for now.
- Self-updates of the launcher itself should stay full downloads too: replacing a running
  binary through the restart helper is risky enough without changing its download path.

## Notes

- MD4 here would only be a content matcher for zsync compatibility, never the security check.

title: [Feature Request] Delta updates for Windows portable zips (central-directory + CRC, no server changes)
author: PanDuroDev
body:
## Motivation

Same as #320: every Craft app ships nearly daily, and each Windows update re-downloads the
full installer. The Linux side is covered by #320/#321 (zsync for AppImages). This issue is
about Windows.

## Why not MSI patches

Windows Installer patches (`.msp`) were considered and dropped on purpose: they are built by
diffing a baseline MSI against the new MSI, need both MSIs plus all source files at build
time, a patch matrix per baseline (or chained patches with bad UX), and signing — on top of
daily releases. Even WiX experts generally recommend major upgrades over patching. MSI
updates should stay full downloads.

## Proposal: central-directory delta against the retained installer

No published delta metadata is needed. A ZIP carries everything required inside itself
(precedent: the `remozipsy` Rust crate and several remote-zip tools work exactly this way).
One subtlety found during validation: comparing against the installed unzipped files is not
enough, because re-compressing them locally would not reproduce the original bytes. The
delta must copy compressed ranges from the previous installer, so the launcher retains one
previous installer per portable install:

- Two small Range requests fetch the tail: End-of-Central-Directory record, then the
  Central Directory itself (names, offsets, sizes, CRC32 per file; every entry is
  compressed independently). Verified against a real published portable zip (10 entries,
  deflated, sane offsets).
- Entries matching by name, CRC32, compressed size and method are copied byte-exact from
  the retained zip; everything else (including every new local header, which is tiny) is
  range-fetched. Local blocks are concatenated in order, the directory tail is copied
  verbatim, and the assembly is SHA-256-verified exactly like a full download (#90 stays
  untouched).
- Unsupported methods, any parse failure, any Range refusal, or any checksum mismatch
  falls back to today's full download. Pause and cancel propagate …

title: [Feature Request] Delta updates for macOS apps (per-release patch for the .app bundle)
author: PanDuroDev
body:
## Motivation

Same as #320: every Craft app ships nearly daily, and each macOS update re-downloads the
full `.dmg`. The Linux side is covered by #320/#321 (zsync for AppImages). This issue is
about macOS.

## Why there is no client-only path (checked)

Unlike ZIP, a `.dmg` (UDIF) carries no per-chunk content hashes in its footer, so unchanged
blocks cannot be identified without server-published metadata. The AppImage `.zsync` files
have no macOS equivalent in current releases (verified on the latest PhotoCraft, FigCraft
and WordCraft assets). So macOS genuinely needs a build-side artifact.

## Proposal

Publish a binary patch per release for the `.app` bundle (e.g. xdelta/VCDIFF, RFC 3284, an
open standard ΓÇö Sparkle-style but without needing Sparkle.framework since the apps are pure
Rust):

- The launcher downloads the patch, applies it to the installed copy in `/Applications`,

- No matching installed copy, no patch listed, or any failure: fall back to today's full
  `.dmg`, which stays the container for fresh installs. Pause and cancel propagate

MSIX packages are ZIPs with a published block map (~64 KiB blocks), which enables exactly

title: macOS: quitting crashes (_NSTouchBarFinderObservation)
author: jmacek
body:
ArtCraft Launcher 0.4.0 crashes on macOS when it quits. I hit it right after updating; Thread 7 in the crash report was waiting on a process the Launcher had spawned. It's the same crash as storytold/craft-libs#3:

```
-[_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate]
___NSTouchBarFinderSetNeedsUpdateOnMain_block_invoke_2
NSDisplayCycleFlush
-[NSApplication run]
eframe::run_native_ext
```

Tested on a MacBookPro17,1 with macOS 26.5.2. The same crash also happens on Macs without a Touch Bar (storytold/pdfcraft#1136).

**Repro:** open the Launcher and, with its window in front, pretend to be a newer Launcher:
```bash
printf 'artcraft-launcher:hello 9.9.9' | nc -w 3 127.0.0.1 47413
```
It quits to hand over to the "newer" version and crashes with EXC_BREAKPOINT / SIGTRAP. Quit from the tray icon didn't crash in my one try, but it goes through the same path. On a MacBook Pro without a Touch Bar it crashed with the window in the background too (see #335).

**Cause:** every real quit (tray Quit, a newer Launcher taking over, self-update) goes through `quit()`, which sends `ViewportCommand::Close` (`apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs`). eframe then drops the window inside AppKit's run loop.

**Possible fix:** `craft-quit` from craft-libs (storytold/craft-libs#5): call `craft_quit::on_close_request(ctx)` at the end of `Shell::logic`. Close-to-tray is unaffected, because it sends `CancelClose` first and `on_close_request` leaves those alone. PdfCraft is adopting it in storytold/pdfcraft#1533.

Related: #215 (make X quit on macOS). Doing that without this fix would make every close crash.

title: Cannot run MSI installer from symlink directory (fails with error 1620)
author: yvvw
body:
### Problem Description

When managing tools or installations via package managers like [Scoop](https://scoop.sh/) (which rely heavily on NTFS symbolic links and directory junctions for data persistence and version management), running `.msi` installers from within a symlinked directory fails https://github.com/ScoopInstaller/Extras/issues/18990.

The Windows Installer aborts with:
> `The Windows Installer stopped with error 1620` (`ERROR_INSTALL_PACKAGE_INVALID`)

### Root Cause

- **Reparse Point / OLE Compound Storage Limitations:** `.msi` packages are OLE Structured Storage files. Windows Installer (`msiexec.exe`) runs under the `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM` service context and invokes legacy storage APIs (like `StgOpenStorage`) which fail to properly resolve or access files through NTFS symlinks/reparse points.
- **Verification:**
  - **Fails:** Invoking `msiexec` with the MSI path pointing through the symlinked directory (e.g. `~\scoop\apps\...`).
  - **Works:** Invoking `msiexec` using the resolved target/canonical path in the persistent directory.

### Proposed Solution

Before invoking `msiexec.exe` to execute the `.msi` file, resolve the file's target path to its canonical physical path.

title: [Feature Request] Choose where portable apps install (default, next to the launcher, custom folder)
author: PanDuroDev
body:
## Motivation

From the follow-up on #316: truly portable setups live wherever the user puts them — a
launcher on `F:\CraftApps` with apps beside it as `F:\CraftApps\<App>`, ready to survive a
Windows reinstall from a separate drive. Today a portable install goes to one fixed place
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`), with no choice offered.

## Proposal

An install-location choice in Settings (Windows, portable installs only — an MSI goes where
the Windows Installer puts it, so the row stays hidden unless portable is selected):

- **Default location**: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`, today's behaviour, still the default.
- **Next to the launcher**: apps install beside the launcher's own executable, so the whole
  setup (launcher + apps) travels together on any drive — the `F:\CraftApps` layout.
- **Custom folder**: an absolute path typed or picked with a Browse button (native folder
  picker, no new dependency). A relative or otherwise unusable path fails the install with
  a clear message instead of silently falling back somewhere else.

Safety properties (same gate as the portable work):

- The install record pins the folder actually used, so removal takes exactly it even after
  the setting changes later; records from before stay valid against the default.
- Detection needs no changes: the record's absolute path covers custom folders, the
  existing folder probe covers the default.
- Updates keep working: the record already drives "same format as installed", and the
  folder travels with it.

## Notes

- A prototype of this (plus the portable install path it needs) is built and field-tested
  locally on real Windows; PR to follow separately so #334 stays reviewable.

_Note: drafted with AI assistance (Muse Spark); posted for discussion._

title: [Bug] Close button does not respond at the top-right screen corner on Windows

## Description

When the ArtCraft Launcher window is maximized on Windows 11, the close button does not respond to clicks when the mouse cursor is positioned at the very top-right corner of the screen.

Moving the cursor slightly to the left or downward makes the close button clickable again.

This suggests that the clickable area (hitbox) of the close button does not extend all the way to the screen corner, possibly due to the rounded button or window geometry.

1. Open ArtCraft Launcher on Windows 11.
2. Maximize the application window.

4. Click the left mouse button.

7. The close button now works.

## Expected Behavior

The close button should respond to clicks anywhere within its designated area, including the extreme top-right corner of the screen when the window is maximized.

This is consistent with standard Windows window controls and Fitts's Law, which makes screen edges and corners particularly convenient mouse targets.

## Actual Behavior

The extreme top-right corner appears to be outside the close button's clickable area, requiring the user to move the cursor slightly inward before clicking.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Application: ArtCraft Launcher
- Window state: Maximized

## Additional Context

The visible close button itself works correctly. The issue appears to be limited to its clickable area at the screen corner.

author: tydude001
body:
Follow-up from #370, as @dylanmtaylor suggested.

The "ArtCraft Launcher {version} is available." dialog has one line of text, whichever button it shows:

> A new version is available. Would you like to relaunch with the updated version?

(`launcher_update_dialog`, `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:116` on `main`.)

That fits **Update and restart**. But when the copy can't update itself (`Capabilities::self_update` false), the dialog shows **Download** instead. Download opens the new release's download link in the browser and closes the dialog, and nothing relaunches. On Linux that applies to every copy that isn't an AppImage or a `.deb`/`.rpm` install in `/usr/bin`, and to any sandboxed copy (`self_update::detect`): the Flatpak and a `.tar.gz` copy, for example. It also applies on FreeBSD. Seen in the 0.4.0 Flatpak with 0.4.1 out.

A fix would be a second sentence for the Download case, something like "Download it to replace this version?". The string has translations in 10 `.tsv` catalogs, so the new sentence would need them too.

title: Windows: launcher selects the discrete GPU and ignores the Power saving preference
author: Bajahaw
body:
## What happens

On a hybrid laptop the launcher keeps the discrete NVIDIA GPU awake, even when Windows Graphics settings say Power saving for this exact executable.

Machine: ASUS Vivobook M6500RE, Windows 11 (build 26100), AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics + NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU. Launcher 0.4.1, installed at `C:\Users\radhi\AppData\Local\Programs\ArtCraft Launcher\artcraft-launcher.exe`.

Windows Settings, System, Display, Graphics, ArtCraft Launcher is set to **Power saving (AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics)**. That is stored as `GpuPreference=1` under `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\DirectX\UserGpuPreferences` for that path.

The running process still opens the NVIDIA driver (`nvwgf2umx.dll`, `nvgpucomp64.dll`, `nvldumdx.dll`) and is the only process `nvidia-smi` lists:

- type C+G, utilization 0%, memory 0 MiB, power state P8
- the chip draws about 8 W instead of powering off

The panel is driven by the AMD GPU (`Disp.A` is Off on the NVIDIA adapter). Nothing else is holding the discrete GPU. Quitting the launcher is what lets it sleep. The Power saving dropdown does not.

8 W idle is most of this laptop's battery discharge while the launcher is just sitting open (total discharge was about 14 W, of which the NVIDIA chip was 8 W and the AMD package about 4 W).

## Why

`wgpu_options()` on Windows installs its own adapter selector and does not ask DXGI which GPU Windows prefers. `adapter_rank` in `apps/artcraft-launcher/src/main.rs` orders adapters like this:

```rust
DeviceType::DiscreteGpu => 1 + u8::from(integrated),
DeviceType::IntegratedGpu => 2 - u8::from(integrated),
```

`integrated` is true only when `power_preference` is already `PowerPreference::LowPower`. The Windows path never sets that. egui-wgpu 0.36 defaults it to `HighPerformance` unless `WGPU_POWER_PREF` is set (`WgpuSetupCreateNew::without_display_handle`). With a `native_adapter_selector` installed, egui ignores `power_preference` and uses this rank, so the discrete GPU wins.

title: [Bug]: Flatpak version downloads AppImage instead of triggering Flatpak/in-place update
author: danflood94
body:
When running ArtCraft Craft-Launcher installed via Flatpak, clicking the Update notification/button causes the launcher to download a standalone .AppImage file to the filesystem rather than updating the Flatpak package or delegating update management to the host/Flatpak runtime.

**Steps to Reproduce**

- Install and launch CraftLauncher via Flatpak.
- Wait for an update banner or notification stating "Update available".
- Click the Update (or Download Update) button.
- Observe the download action and destination directory (e.g., ~/Downloads data path).


**Expected Behavior**

Because the application is packaged and running inside a Flatpak sandbox:

-  It should either delegate updates to Flatpak / software center (flatpak update), OR
-  If self-updating from within the sandbox, it should fetch Flatpak-compatible runtime bundles rather than dropping a raw Linux .AppImage.
-  At minimum, the UI should indicate: "An update is available via Flatpak. Please run flatpak update or use your software center." instead of defaulting to the generic Linux AppImage download pipeline.

**Actual Behavior**

The launcher detects the Linux OS environment, queries release assets, and blindly pulls the .AppImage binary, leaving the user with an unintegrated standalone executable that cannot update the active Flatpak installation.

title: Portable-zip delta can never reuse entries while every entry name embeds the version
author: PanDuroDev
body:
Field-testing the portable work in #345, a PhotoCraft 0.8.2 to 0.9.0 update logged `nothing reusable; a full download is cheaper` and fell back. I checked whether that claim is true or a matcher bug, against the actual published zips (downloaded, compared locally, no repo changes):

- Both zips hold 9 entries. Every entry path starts with a versioned top folder: `photocraft-0.8.2-windows-x64-portable/photocraft.exe` vs `photocraft-0.9.0-windows-x64-portable/photocraft.exe`.
- Compared by the exact `plan()` criteria (name plus CRC32 plus compressed size plus method): 0 common names out of 9 plus 9. Reuse is mathematically impossible here, whatever the content. The log told the truth; the matcher (exact names) is correct code against inputs that defeat it.

So the portable delta as designed is inert for these zips: the installer already flattens the single versioned top folder away, but the delta matcher compares the full names. One honest caveat on payoff: even with relative matching, 0.8.2 to 0.9.0 would only have reused the small identical files (licenses), since the ~80 MB executable changed anyway. The saving shows up on small-change releases, which this release cadence does produce.

Maintainer decision requested, two options:
1. Match by path relative to the single shared top folder (validation still on full names; both zips already require exactly one top folder at install), or
2. Consciously keep full downloads for portable and document the delta as best-effort for stable names.

Which do you prefer? Happy to implement option 1 in #345 if wanted, or leave it.

Field evidence: PhotoCraft 0.8.2 to 0.9.0 portable update succeeded via fallback (no UAC, flat layout, no portable.txt, manifest root pinned, single .kept base rotated). guntisratkevics field-tested the earlier revision (see #345).

_Note: drafted with AI assistance (Muse Spark)._

title: Uninstall leaves the retained installer (.kept) behind; propose an explicit complete removal
author: PanDuroDev
body:
Uninstalling a portable app removes its folder, shortcut and manifest record, but the retained installer under `downloads/.kept/<app>/` stays forever: nothing ever deletes it (no UI action, no prune on uninstall, no expiry - it is only replaced by a newer base on the next install, or removed by hand). For an 80 MB app, uninstalling to free space silently keeps 80 MB.

Field case from testing #345: after uninstalling PhotoCraft, reinstalling the same version assembled the zip from the kept base in seconds (only headers crossed the network). That instant reinstall is the upside of keeping the base - so silently deleting it on every uninstall would also destroy a real benefit.

Proposal (maintainer decision requested): keep the current uninstall as-is (fast reinstall), and add an explicit second action, e.g. `Remove completely`, that also deletes the kept base. Alternatives: surface kept bases with their sizes and a discard control (paused downloads already have one), or auto-delete the base on uninstall with a note. Which do you prefer?

Related: #345 (retention), #423 (delta matching).

_Note: drafted with AI assistance (Muse Spark)._

title: [Feature Request] [Linux] In-app source compilation option for Arch Linux and non-deb/rpm distros
author: mightymisanthrope
body:
### Summary
Add an option to compile and install apps from source directly within ArtCraft Launcher, providing a first-class native installation and update path for Arch Linux and other distributions that lack pre-built `.deb` or `.rpm` packages.

### Current Behavior
- On Arch Linux, the default system package installer attempts to invoke `.rpm` (see #115, #61) or falls back to Flatpak/AppImage.
- Existing AUR or source installs are marked as `managed_elsewhere`, which disables in-app updates and directs the user to open a terminal and run `yay -S <pkg>` manually.

### Proposed Solution
1. **"Build / Update from Source" Action**: Allow users to compile apps locally via `cargo` directly into `~/.local/bin` and register desktop entries in `~/.local/share/applications` without needing root/sudo permissions.
2. **Crate Progress in UI**: Use Cargo's `--message-format=json` artifact stream to show real crate-by-crate progress (`done/total` crates and estimated time) in the launcher window during active builds.
3. **Artifact Hygiene & Provenance Tracking**:
   - Strip and copy final release binaries (including companion CLI targets) to `~/.local/bin`, then prune intermediate `target/` build artifacts so disk usage stays minimal.
   - Record an install manifest (commit SHA, branch, installed binaries) under `InstallKind::Source` so launcher-built binaries support first-class in-app updates and uninstallation rather than being flagged as `managed_elsewhere`.
4. **Flexible Selection & Smart Fallback**:

title: Flaky test on Linux: reads_binary_version_when_the_cli_uses_the_display_name_or_a_former_id fails with "Text file busy"
author: abszar
body:
### What happens

`detect::linux_tests::reads_binary_version_when_the_cli_uses_the_display_name_or_a_former_id` (`crates/native/src/detect.rs`) fails at random: about 1 run in 5 of `cargo test -p artcraft-launcher-native --lib`, then passes when re-run. When it fails:

```
panicked at crates/native/src/detect.rs:479:90:
called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
```

### Cause (confirmed)

I made the test print the error from `process::run` when it fails. It caught this on the 4th loop:

```
couldn't start /tmp/.tmpg7Q1wL/soundcraft (Text file busy (os error 26))
```

The test writes a shell script, makes it executable and runs it straight away. Tests run in parallel threads. If another thread forks to start a process while the script's file is still open for writing, the child briefly inherits that write descriptor. Until the child execs, the kernel refuses to run the script, with `ETXTBSY`. `capture` turns the error into `None`, so `binary_version` returns `None` and the `unwrap` panics.

The test just above it (writing a script at `detect.rs:463`) has the same pattern.

### Suggested fix

In the tests' `write` helper, retry running the script for a short bounded time while the error is `ETXTBSY` (`ErrorKind::ExecutableFileBusy`, or raw os error 26). Or make the two script tests share one mutex with nothing else spawning processes at that moment. The retry is the usual fix and keeps the tests parallel.

It might be worth checking whether production code has the same window. `install.rs` and `self_update.rs` also write an executable and may run it while other threads start processes. I haven't checked whether they run it immediately.

### Environment

Ubuntu 24.04 (X11), `main` at 0f295d4, Rust 1.97.

title: macOS: v0.3.2 fails to update apps from a standard user account without requesting administrator authorization
author: JeromeMorow
body:
ArtCraft Launcher v0.3.2 cannot update installed ArtCraft apps in `/Applications` when running under a standard, non-admin macOS account. This affects multiple ArtCraft apps, including PhotoCraft.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Sign in to macOS with a standard user account that is not a member of the `admin` group.
2. Open ArtCraft Launcher v0.3.2 with an ArtCraft app already installed in `/Applications`.
3. Attempt to update the app.

### Actual behavior
The update fails with:
```text
couldn't copy the app: ditto: /Applications/.PhotoCraft.app.partial: Permission denied
```
No macOS administrator authorization prompt appears.

### Diagnostic findings
- `/Applications` has permissions and ownership `drwxrwxr-x root admin`.
- The standard user is not a member of the `admin` group, as expected.
- Enabling Full Disk Access for the launcher as a troubleshooting step did not resolve the problem.
- Multiple ArtCraft apps are affected; this is not specific to PhotoCraft.

The observed behavior suggests that the update process attempts to write to `/Applications` without obtaining the required privileges.

### Expected behavior
When updating an app in `/Applications` requires elevated privileges, the launcher should request macOS administrator authorization and use an appropriate privileged installation mechanism.

Updates should work from a standard user account without changing `/Applications` permissions or granting the everyday user permanent administrator privileges.

title: [Linux] Launcher aborts at startup on VNC X server: DRI3 BadMatch/BadDrawable surfaces as XMapRaised panic
author: mushketer888
body:
## Description

The launcher (0.4.1, Flatpak) cannot start a window on a VNC-backed X11 session. It aborts during startup: an async DRI3 X11 error is picked up at window-map time and escalated through winit into a non-unwinding panic, so the process dies (and, per the single-instance lock noted in #69, a stale process can also block relaunching).

PhotoCraft (0.7.0, same machine, same display, same Flatpak runtime family) opens its window fine, so this is launcher/wgpu-surface specific, not a totally GPU-less box.

## Logs

Default backend (Vulkan, adapter auto):

```
[INFO  artcraft_launcher] ArtCraft Launcher 0.4.1, ...
[WARN  artcraft_launcher] no tray icon: D-Bus connection error: ... ServiceUnknown: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown
[ERROR winit::platform_impl::linux] X11 error: XError {
        description: "BadMatch (invalid parameter attributes)",
        error_code: 8,
        request_code: 149,
        minor_code: 4,
    }
... (repeats 3x)
[ERROR artcraft_launcher::logging] internal error: panicked at winit-0.30.13/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/window.rs:1145:41:
    Failed to call XMapRaised: XError { description: "BadMatch ...", error_code: 8, request_code: 149, minor_code: 4 }
[ERROR artcraft_launcher::logging] internal error: panicked at winit-0.30.13/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/window.rs:586:34:
    called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: PoisonError { .. }
[ERROR artcraft_launcher::logging] internal error: panicked at library/core/src/panicking.rs:233:5:
    panic in a destructor during cleanup
thread caused non-unwinding panic. aborting.
```

Request 149 on this server is **DRI3** (verified via `xdpyinfo -queryExtensions`), so the window-map call is just the messenger for an earlier async DRI3 failure. Even `--help` takes this path (a window is created unconditionally at startup).

## Environment

- Launcher: artcraft-launcher-0.4.1-linux-x86_64.flatpak (`flatpak install --user`), also reproduced on 0.2.1
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04-based, kernel …

title: Request: Add the option "Ask for administrator privileges once for each batch of operations" for the Craft Apps batch update system
author: VINTSPECT
body: I got this idea from the "[UniGetUI](https://github.com/Devolutions/UniGetUI)" software, which has a feature to "Ask for administrator privileges once for each batch of operations." This means that if we’re performing batch updates or updating more than one application at the same time (for example, 10 batch software updates), we only need to confirm the request for administrator permissions once in the Windows installer wizard, so we don’t have to click “Confirm” 10 times for the 10 updated software packages. This option is available in the UniGetUI settings menu (see attached image). (I’m using UniGetUI version 3.3.7) Based on this feature, my request is to implement it into Craft Apps Manager. I believe this could be a great feature because every time I update more than one Craft App, each one displays an administrator permission prompt, which I find inefficient. If I update 12 Craft Apps, I have to click the administrator permission confirmation button 12 times. With the option “Ask for administrator privileges once for each batch of operations,” I can save time because I only need to click the confirmation once and then wait for everything to finish updating without having to click the confirmation repeatedly. Thank you. I hope my request will be considered. Best regards.

title: [Linux/ChromeOS] Apps fall back to llvmpipe on Crostini: user lacks access to /dev/dri/renderD128 (render group) — workaround inside
author: ojtvpn
body:
## Summary

On ChromeOS Linux (Crostini), Craft apps fall back to the software renderer (`llvmpipe`) and show "graphics card not detected / slower" even though the container has a working GPU (virtio-gpu → Intel). Under CPU load this shows up as heavy flickering and an unresponsive window.

**Cause:** the GPU render node `/dev/dri/renderD128` is owned by group `render`, but the default Crostini user is not in that group (it is in `video`). Vulkan and Wayland EGL cannot open the GPU, so wgpu picks `llvmpipe`.

This probably also explains other ChromeOS/Googlebook reports, e.g. storytold/lightcraft#973.

## Environment

- ChromeOS, built-in Debian 13 Linux container (Crostini), x86_64
- GPU: Intel Alder Lake GT2, exposed as `Virtio-GPU Venus` (Vulkan) / `virgl` (GL)
- Mesa 25.0.7-2+deb13u1
- PdfCraft 0.8.0, GridCraft 0.7.0, ArtCraft Launcher 0.4.1 (official .deb)

## Diagnosis

```
$ ls -l /dev/dri/renderD128
crw-rw---- 1 root render 226, 128 ... /dev/dri/renderD128
$ id
... groups=...,44(video),...,993(kvm)        # no "render"

$ vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName
deviceName = llvmpipe (LLVM 19.1.7, 256 bits)
```

PdfCraft log before the fix:
```
WARN egui_wgpu: Software rasterizer detected - loss of performance expected. backend: Vulkan, device_type: Cpu, name: "llvmpipe (LLVM 19.1.7, 256 bits)"
INFO pdfcraft: renderer: wgpu; adapter: llvmpipe (LLVM 19.1.7, 256 bits) (Cpu, Vulkan)
```

## Workaround

Give your user access to the render node. Option A works immediately with no restart:

```bash
# A) let the "video" group (which the Crostini user and sommelier/Xwayland already have) use the render node
sudo chgrp video /dev/dri/renderD128
echo 'SUBSYSTEM=="drm", KERNEL=="renderD*", GROUP="video", MODE="0660"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/70-crostini-render-video.rules

# B) or add yourself to "render", then fully restart Linux (right-click Terminal → "Shut down Linux")
sudo usermod -aG render $USER
```

After the fix:
```
$ vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName
…

title: [Feature Request] Deduplicate shared assets and runtime components across Craft apps
author: zhongwei
body:
Problem

The Craft apps are distributed as independent packages, which may result in shared assets or runtime components being duplicated across multiple installations.

For example, PhotoCraft's official desktop builds embed fonts from the shared craft-fonts repository at build time. Other Craft apps use similar build-time resource embedding.

Sharing these components at installation time could reduce download sizes and disk usage, especially for users who install multiple Craft apps.

Proposal

Introduce an optional shared-components installation model managed centrally by ArtCraft Launcher.

The launcher could:

Detect shared components required by installed apps.

Download and install common assets, such as fonts, icons, and other suitable resources, only once.

Manage component versions, compatibility, updates, and cleanup.

Track which apps depend on each shared component.

Show users the potential download and disk-space savings.

Where technically appropriate, the same approach could be considered for shared runtime libraries. However, this should be evaluated separately from sharing static assets.

Standalone app packages should remain available for portable, offline, and independent installation scenarios.

Cross-project coordination and implementation

This change would likely require coordinated work across multiple repositories rather than changes to ArtCraft Launcher alone.

ArtCraft Launcher should serve as the central entry point and coordinator, while the relevant app and shared-component projects participate in defining and implementing the necessary changes.

Potential areas of work include:

title: Launcher exits on startup on Intel Iris (Mac mini Late 2014): Metal compiler error in wgpu indirect validation
author: pauerbuk
body:
## Description

ArtCraft Launcher 0.4.1 quits immediately after launch on a Mac mini (Late 2014). The window briefly appears and then the app exits. No log file is written to `~/Library/Application Support/ArtCraft Launcher/logs/` and no crash report is generated.

## Environment

- ArtCraft Launcher: 0.4.1 (universal DMG)
- Mac: Mac mini (Late 2014), Intel Iris Graphics
- macOS: Monterey 12.x

## Log

Running the binary from Terminal with `RUST_LOG=debug` shows that the Metal shader compiler fails on wgpu's indirect-validation compute pipeline, which causes the device to be lost:

```
wgpu_core::instance] Adapter AdapterInfo { name: "Intel Iris Graphics", ..., device_type: IntegratedGpu, backend: Metal, ... }
wgpu_core::indirect_validation] indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("new_compute_pipeline_state: NSError { code: 2, localizedDescription: \"Compiler encountered an internal error\", domain: \"CompilerError\", ... }"))
eframe::native::run] Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
artcraft_launcher] WGPU error: Parent device is lost
```

## Workaround

Disabling wgpu indirect-call validation via environment variable makes the launcher start and work normally:

```
WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=0 "/Applications/ArtCraft Launcher.app/Contents/MacOS/ArtCraft Launcher"
```

With this, I was able to install VectorCraft 0.12.0 and PhotoCraft from the launcher, and both run fine.

## Suggestion

It might help to disable `InstanceFlags::VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` in release builds, or fall back gracefully when the indirect-validation pipeline fails to compile, so older Intel GPUs on macOS can still run the launcher and the Craft apps.

Description

title: Publish the suite catalog (SUITE) as data so downstream tooling need not parse catalog.rs
author: zberry
body:
## Context

`crates/core/src/catalog.rs` (`pub const SUITE`) is the authoritative list of Craft apps: new apps appear there first. Downstream tooling that builds every app from source has no way to notice a new app other than to fetch that Rust file from GitHub and pull the `"storytold/<id>"` strings out of the `SUITE` block with a regular expression. That works today (it spotted figcraft the day it was added) but any refactor of the file, a renamed constant, or a repo string built at runtime would silently break it.

## Proposal

Keep the data in one place that is both what the launcher compiles and what tools can read. Two shapes that would work, in order of preference:

1. A `catalog.json` (or TOML) in the repo that `catalog.rs` includes at compile time (`include_str!` plus a `serde` parse in a `build.rs` or a `LazyLock`), so the Rust constant and the published data cannot drift.
2. The current Rust source as is, plus a generated `catalog.json` that CI checks is in sync (`cargo xtask catalog --check`) and that gets attached to each launcher release.

Fields that matter downstream: app id, repository (`owner/name`), display title, and whether the app is released for Linux. We are happy to send the PR for either shape.

title: [Bug] Crash on startup on macOS Monterey (Intel Mac): WGPU error - Parent device is lost / Compiler encountered an internal error
author: messor-sketch
body:
### Describing the bug
The ArtCraft Launcher crashes instantly on startup on macOS Monterey (Intel MacBook Pro). The application icon bounces in the Dock and closes immediately without rendering any window or interface.

Running the executable directly via the Terminal reveals a critical graphics initialization crash related to `wgpu` and Apple's Metal compiler.

### To Reproduce
1. Download the latest version of ArtCraft Launcher on macOS Monterey (Intel).
2. Launch the application.
3. The icon bounces in the Dock and crashes immediately.

### Terminal Error Output
When forcing the execution via the Terminal using `sudo /Applications/ArtCraft\ Launcher.app/Contents/MacOS/ArtCraft\ Launcher`, the following log is produced:

```text
[2026-10-18T19:19:25Z ERROR wgpu_core::indirect_validation] indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("new_compute_pipeline_state: NSError { code: 2, localizedDescription: \"Compiler encountered an internal error\", domain: \"CompilerError\", userInfo: {\"NSLocalizedDescription\": <__NSCFString: 0x600001013380>}, .. }"))
[2026-10-18T19:19:25Z ERROR eframe::native::run] Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
[2026-10-18T19:19:25Z ERROR artcraft_launcher] WGPU error: Parent device is lost
```

Trying to force alternative backends using `WGPU_BACKEND=gl` results in:
```text
[2026-10-18T19:21:14Z ERROR eframe::native::run] Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Failed to create surface for any enabled backend: {}
```

### Environment:
- **OS:** macOS Monterey 12.x
- **Hardware:** Intel MacBook Pro
- **Graphics Engine:** `wgpu` / `eframe` (Rust)

### Additional Context
This seems to be a compatibility issue between newer `wgpu` compute pipeline shaders and older integrated Intel Iris/HD graphics drivers on macOS Monterey, causing the Metal compiler to trigger an internal error.
